bilingual_context: English/French bilingualism is a genuine differentiator in the NCR — for federal government, Crown corporations, and many customer-facing roles. If you are bilingual, state it with your working level.
public_sector_context: Federal departments, agencies, and Crown corporations hire many student and new-grad business roles (FSWEP, co-op, policy, procurement, finance). They value documentation quality, process discipline, stakeholder coordination, and bilingualism.
b2b_tech_context: The Kanata North area hosts a large concentration of B2B technology companies (telecom, SaaS, cybersecurity, semiconductors). Their business roles are B2B: longer sales cycles, technical products, CRM discipline, and close marketing-sales-product collaboration.
positioning_advice: Ottawa's market is mostly B2B and public-sector, not consumer brands — position your evidence around stakeholders, documentation, and process rather than consumer buzz.
If you are bilingual (or in French Immersion), make it explicit — it materially widens your NCR options.
Local student experience (uOttawa/Carleton clubs, NCR non-profits, government student programs) is recognized by Ottawa employers — name organizations rather than genericizing them.

role_angles.advice: For an Ottawa/Kanata B2B technology role, make technical curiosity, CRM usage, campaign or pipeline reporting, documentation, and cross-functional (sales-marketing-product) communication clearly visible on your resume.

For a public-sector or Crown-corporation role in the NCR, emphasize bilingual communication (if applicable), documentation quality, stakeholder coordination, and reliable process work — these are weighted heavily.
Ottawa has a dense non-profit and association sector — fundraising, sponsorship, event, and volunteer-coordination evidence from student life transfers directly; quantify it.
